meta.reportLabel: THE HAVEN FAILURE IS NOW A COMMODITY FAILURE TOO - and that is today's change. Yesterday gold and the franc refused to bid on the biggest escalation of the war. Today the INDUSTRIAL metals joined them: copper fell 1.00% to 6.7356 USD per pound and its monthly gain collapsed to +1.87% from +2.90% on the week, silver fell 0.94% to 66.634, and gold broke BELOW 4,400 to 4,392.69 with only +0.54% left on the month. Meanwhile crude went the other way again - WTI 97.269 and +1.27% today for +16.85% on the month, Brent 102.167. Energy is now the ONLY asset carrying the war premium, and the reason the metals are cracking is the Fed: CME FedWatch has drifted to 58% from 56% for a September 16 hike, with TE forecasting 4.00%. Rising US real rates beat the haven bid. That costs AUD its commodity leg (score held at +2 on the rate differential alone, NOT on copper) and forces one bias change: XAG/USD is DOWNGRADED from LONG to RANGE, joining gold. UK gas got worse again at +38.71% monthly, the worst in G10. Board unchanged: JPY +3; AUD +2; EUR, USD, CAD, CHF +1; GBP -1, NZD -1. Cleanest: NZD/JPY SHORT, GBP/JPY SHORT, JPYBASKET LONG, USD/JPY SHORT, AUD/NZD LONG, EUR/GBP LONG, USOIL LONG. ECB TODAY 12:15Z, US PPI 12:30Z, US CPI tomorrow.

meta.regime: The war premium has stopped being a cross-asset risk premium and become a pure ENERGY premium. Crude is +16.85% on the month and Brent holds above 102, while gold has broken below 4,400 with only +0.54% left on the month, silver is falling and copper has now turned down too. The transmission channel is US real rates: with CME FedWatch at 58% for a September 16 hike and TE forecasting 4.00%, the discount rate on every non-yielding haven is rising faster than the war can bid them. That leaves FX trading pure monetary-policy differentials, which is why the yen - the one currency with a central bank the market has already priced into a hike - is still the only clean directional trade on the board. The second feature is unchanged: Europe is absorbing an energy tax it cannot hedge while its central bank tightens into it, and rate futures keep a December ECB hike alive at roughly 40-50%.
meta.nextBigEvent: The ECB TODAY, September 10 at 12:15Z, with the press conference at 12:45Z. The 25bp to a 2.50% deposit facility is 99% priced - TE carries consensus and forecast at 2.65% on the refi - and every one of the 65 economists in the September 3 Reuters poll expects it, so the move is not the event. The event is the NEW STAFF PROJECTIONS. August energy inflation jumped to 14.3% from 10.3% and headline HICP hit 3.3%, the highest since September 2023, with core at 2.4%. Since those numbers were collected, EU gas has risen further to 80.30 euros per MWh, German gas jumped 4.42% in a single session to 80.40, and German storage sits at only 53% full. The staff inflation path can therefore be revised UP into a market that had decided the cycle was finished. TE states directly that interest-rate futures are pricing a THIRD hike by December while policymakers keep flagging upside inflation risks - but also that the ECB is expected to signal CAUTION about further increases that could weigh on activity, that there is still little evidence of the second-round effects policymakers fear, and that economists warn more tightening risks recession. Lagarde retaining full optionality is the hawkish outcome; naming 2.50% as terminal is the dovish one. US PPI lands 15 minutes later at 12:30Z and August CPI tomorrow at 12:30Z is the bigger number for the whole board.

dailyRead: Yesterday this file said the biggest escalation of the war produced almost no FX haven bid, and that the board was therefore trading central banks rather than the war. Today that observation extends into the metals complex and gets a cleaner explanation. Copper fell 1.00% to 6.7356 USD per pound, cutting its monthly gain to +1.87% after being +2.90% on the WEEK only yesterday; silver fell 0.94% to 66.634; and gold broke below 4,400, trading 4,392.69 with a monthly gain of just +0.54%. Set that against crude, which went the other way for a second session: WTI 97.269, +1.27% today and +16.85% on the month, with Brent 102.167 and +14.82%. Energy is the only asset class still paying the war premium. The mechanism is US real rates. CME FedWatch has drifted to 58% from 56% for a September 16 hike after August payrolls at +162,000 against +53,000 expected, and TradingEconomics now forecasts 4.00% outright; a rising discount rate beats a geopolitical bid on every asset that pays no coupon, which is precisely why gold and silver are falling in the middle of a shooting war. Two disciplined caveats belong here. First, 56% to 58% is a two-point drift and CoinDesk argued on September 7 that the payrolls print did NOT materially move Fed pricing - so the USD score does not flip on it, and August CPI tomorrow at 12:30Z is the number that decides September 16. Second, one session of copper weakness does not break the Australian thesis: AUD holds at +2 on the G10-high 4.35% cash rate with September 29 near 54% priced, on inflation expectations stuck at 4.9%, and on trimmed mean at 3.6% - NOT on the commodity leg, which has now visibly weakened and should stop being cited as support. That distinction is the one that matters for position sizing, and it is why XCU/USD keeps its LONG direction on the genuine supply shortage but loses conviction to LOW-MED. The one outright bias change today is XAG/USD, downgraded from LONG to RANGE. Silver was held as a gold substitute with an extra industrial leg; today it fell harder than gold while copper fell harder still, so the industrial leg is the part that broke and the reason to prefer silver has gone. It joins gold at RANGE. Elsewhere the board is stable and the stability is informative. The yen remains the only uncompromised score at +3 - TE carries consensus AND its own forecast at 1.25% for the September 18 BoJ, board member Masu said the Bank expects to keep raising precisely to avoid being forced into rapid tightening later, average cash earnings are +4.7% y/y and the fastest since 1997, and USD/JPY at 153.716 is still -3.50% on the month even after a +0.11% session. Sterling stays at -1 and its energy problem got worse again: UK gas is 200.38 pence per therm and now +38.71% on the month, up from +36.33% yesterday, the worst gas exposure in G10, into a confirmed October Ofgem cap rise - stagflationary for a Bank of England that TE shows will not move on September 17 and cannot ease either. The kiwi stays at -1 on a central bank that hiked to 2.75% and then declined to validate the next step, with TE carrying October 28 unchanged and the next 25bp only on December 9; NZD/USD at 0.58399 is flat on the day and -0.65% on the month, the worst major. The loonie stays at +1 with the same uncomfortable footnote as yesterday: Brent is above 102 and USD/CAD is 1.38134, up another 0.06%, so the oil beta remains broken and every CAD expression stays low-conviction. And the franc failed its haven test for a SECOND session - USD/CHF 0.81110, +0.12%, leaving CHF flat on the month - so while the Swiss data alone would justify +2, the score stays at +1 and the franc should now be expressed on data and differentials only, never as a haven. Trade the yen, trade crude, trade the AUD/NZD antipodean spread, and let the ECB and tomorrow's CPI resolve the euro and the dollar.

today.headline: ECB decides TODAY at 12:15Z - the hike is 99% priced, so the new staff projections and Lagarde at 12:45Z are the entire event.
today.read: The asymmetry favours a hawkish surprise: August energy inflation was already 14.3% and gas has risen since, so the staff path can be revised UP into a market that thought the cycle was over. Own EUR against GBP and NZD into it, and keep EUR/USD, EUR/CAD and EUR/CHF as ranges until Lagarde speaks.

today.headline: Fed pricing drifted to 58% from 56% for September 16 and TE now forecasts 4.00% - and it is showing up in the metals, not in FX.
today.read: Treat the two-point drift as noise, not a signal: the dollar is dormant until August CPI lands tomorrow at 12:30Z with consensus 3.4%. The tradeable expression of rising US real rates right now is short gold and short silver, not long dollars - DXY is still -1.03% on the month.

today.headline: Copper turned down 1.00% to 6.7356 and its monthly gain halved - the Australian commodity leg has visibly weakened.
today.read: AUD stays at +2 but the support is now the 4.35% cash rate and 4.9% inflation expectations, NOT commodities, so express it against NZD where the rate story is cleanest rather than against USD. A second soft copper session plus another weak domestic print would be the trigger to cut to +1.

today.headline: UK gas worsened again to 200.38 pence, now +38.71% on the month against +36.33% yesterday - the worst energy exposure in G10.
today.read: This tightens the stagflation vice into an October Ofgem cap rise: it lifts the CPI path while cutting real incomes, and TE shows a Bank frozen at 3.75% on September 17 with a 0/9 vote-cut consensus. Keep sterling short against JPY and EUR, not against USD where cable is still +0.32% on the month.

today.headline: Brent above 102 and WTI +16.85% on the month, and USD/CAD went UP again to 1.38134 - the oil beta is still broken.
today.read: Until the loonie starts trading its own terms of trade, keep every CAD expression low-conviction and take the crude view through USOIL directly instead. The next catalyst is a labour stabilisation, not an oil headline - August wages at 2.0% y/y are what is actually capping this currency.

today.headline: Second straight session with no haven bid - USD/CHF 0.81110, +0.12%, leaving the franc flat on the month through the war escalation.
today.read: The haven argument is retired: from here trade CHF only on its data and differentials, which are strong enough to hold +1 but capped by an SNB that forecasts 0.6% inflation and has signalled greater readiness to intervene. Keep every CHF cross at MEDIUM or below into September 24.

today.headline: No change - thesis holds, and it is the only uncompromised score on the board.
today.read: TE carries its own forecast at 1.25% for September 18 against a 1% consensus, so the yen gets paid on guidance and on the roughly 75bp of cumulative tightening swaps carry to April 2027. USD/JPY at 153.716 is still -3.50% on the month; a hike-and-explicit-pause is the only thing that breaks this.

today.headline: No change - and it is now the only major with a NEGATIVE monthly return against the dollar.
today.read: NZD/USD -0.65% on the month confirms that a central bank which hikes to 2.75% and then refuses to validate the next step does not get paid for its carry. Stay short via NZD/JPY and long AUD/NZD; October 28 pulling the December hike forward is the invalidation.

USD.when: Sept 16, 18:00Z - CME FedWatch has drifted to 58% from 56% for a 25bp move to 4.00%, which is also TE's own forecast
USD.note: TE re-verified this morning: policy rate 3.75% upper bound, CPI 3.4% with MoM 0.1%, unemployment 4.1%, non-farm payrolls +162,000 against a prior +21,000, GDP growth rate 1.5% with annual growth 2.1%, business confidence 54.6, manufacturing PMI 53.9, non-manufacturing 55.4, services 56.5, consumer confidence 51.7, retail sales -0.6% m/m, balance of trade -88.58bn, current account -227bn. The one thing that moved is pricing: CME FedWatch is now near 58%, up from 56% yesterday and having been 58.7% on September 7 and 66% on August 31 after Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole remarks. That is a two-point drift inside a range this file has already seen, and CoinDesk argued explicitly on September 7 that the payrolls beat did NOT materially boost hike odds - so it is noise and USD does NOT flip on it. It is worth naming because of where it shows up: in the metals. Gold below 4,400 and silver -0.94% are the rising-real-rate trade, not the risk-appetite trade. TE now forecasts 4.00% outright for September 16 and its summary of the July minutes tilts the same way - officials concerned about persistent inflation, several judging financial conditions possibly not restrictive enough, a small group wanting an immediate hike to reduce the need for larger moves later, inflation risks viewed as tilted to the UPSIDE - though TE notes the meeting predated the cooler employment and inflation data. Prediction markets remain lower at 48-49% and should not be quoted as rate-market pricing. USD HOLDS at +1. Tactical framing unchanged: hold USD/JPY as a JAPAN trade with a neutral dollar leg, not a two-sided differential trade. DXY 98.830, +0.01% today and -1.03% on the month. US PPI TODAY at 12:30Z, August CPI tomorrow at 12:30Z with consensus 3.4% - that is the decider.

EUR.when: TODAY, Sept 10 at 12:15Z - the deposit facility goes to 2.50% from 2.25%, priced at 99%, with TE carrying consensus and forecast at 2.65% on the refi
EUR.note: Deposit facility re-verified on TE at 2.25%, main refi 2.40%, marginal lending 2.65%; TE's calendar shows the September 10 decision with previous 2.4%, consensus 2.65% and forecast 2.65%. EUR HOLDS at +1 with a hawkish forward tilt, and the correction this file made over the last two days stands: it originally called the ECB path CLOSED on the September 3 Reuters poll, in which all 65 economists expected today's move while 91% saw 2.50% as the year-end rate and 78% saw it through mid-2027. TradingEconomics now states directly that INTEREST-RATE FUTURES ARE PRICING A THIRD HIKE BY DECEMBER while policymakers continue to flag upside inflation risks and rising bond yields add uncertainty; previews put December near 40-50%. Rate-market pricing outranks an economist poll, so the path is OPEN and the original call was wrong. The live event today is the NEW STAFF PROJECTIONS. August energy inflation jumped to 14.3% from 10.3%, HICP hit 3.3% - the highest since September 2023 - with core at 2.4%, and gas has risen SINCE those readings were collected: EU gas is 80.30 euros per MWh, +1.34% today and +36.58% on the month, German gas jumped 4.42% in a session to 80.40 and is +29.43% monthly, and German storage is only 53% full with Morgan Stanley lifting its winter TTF forecast to about 85 euros and no Qatari return expected before winter. The staff inflation path can be revised UP. TE also notes the offsetting case: the ECB is expected to signal caution about further increases that could weigh on activity, there are still few signs of the second-round effects policymakers fear when energy prices surge, and economists remain unconvinced further tightening is necessary and warn it risks recession. The gas move is a terms-of-trade TAX on euro-area activity that no hike offsets. TE macro re-verified: Q2 GDP +0.6% q/q and 1.2% y/y, unemployment 6.4%, inflation 3.3% with core 2.4%, manufacturing PMI 52.7 from 51.9, services 51.6, composite 52, wage growth 3.4% from 3.1%, retail sales +0.6% y/y from 1.4%. Own EUR against sterling and the kiwi; keep EUR/USD, EUR/CAD and EUR/CHF as ranges through the meeting. EUR/USD 1.16318, -0.01% today, +0.81% on the month.

GBP.when: Sept 17, 11:00Z - roughly 90% priced for no change at 3.75%, with TE carrying a 0/9 vote-cut consensus and a 3.75% forecast
GBP.note: Bank Rate re-verified on TE at 3.75%, held 6-3 on July 30 with three members voting for 4.00%. GBP HOLDS at MINUS 1 and the energy leg deteriorated for a third consecutive session: UK gas is 200.38 pence per therm, +1.37% today and now +38.71% on the MONTH, up from +36.33% yesterday and +29.82% the day before - comfortably the worst gas exposure in G10 - feeding a confirmed October Ofgem cap rise. That is stagflationary, not hawkish: it lifts the CPI path while cutting real household income. TE's own summary of the July decision describes exactly the trap sterling is in - the Bank expects inflation to RISE again later this year as higher energy costs feed through, sees little evidence of second-round effects, notes weaker labour conditions and still-elevated borrowing costs reducing underlying pressure, and says risks remain tilted to the upside on geopolitical uncertainty while standing ready to tighten if necessary. A central bank that will not move on September 17 and cannot ease either. The structural leg is unchanged: the highest borrowing costs of any G10 developed nation, July government borrowing 69% above the prior year, and a yield advantage that fails to attract capital because it is a risk premium rather than carry. The momentum caveat also stands and should keep being stated - cable is 1.35421, down 0.04% today but still +0.32% on the MONTH, so the short is not paying against the dollar and GBP/USD stays LOW-MED. TE re-verified: CPI 2.9% with core 2.6%, GDP 0.4% q/q from 0.6% with annual growth 1.2% from 0.9%, unemployment 4.9%, employment change +83k from +147k, claimant count -11k, wage growth 4.1% from 4.4%, manufacturing PMI 51.7, services 52.5, composite 52.5, retail sales +1.6% y/y from 3.8%. Express sterling against the YEN and the EURO. UK monthly GDP tomorrow at 06:00Z is the main risk to the position.

JPY.when: Sept 18, 03:00Z - TE's OWN forecast is 1.25% against a 1% consensus, with reports near 80% priced and swaps carrying ~75bp cumulative by April 2027
JPY.note: Policy rate re-verified on TE at 1.00%, the highest since September 1995, held July 31 by 8-1 with Takata dissenting for 1.25%. TE's calendar is the cleanest single fact on this board: consensus 1% but TE FORECAST 1.25% for September 18. JPY HOLDS at +3 and remains the only uncompromised score here. The hawkish stack is now five confirmations deep across four sessions: board member Kazuyuki MASU said the Bank EXPECTS TO CONTINUE raising rates as underlying inflation nears 2% and that further hikes are needed precisely to avoid being FORCED into rapid tightening later, naming Iran-conflict fuel and chemical costs, higher distribution and food costs, greater pass-through from yen depreciation, and AI-related demand as sources of persistent price pressure - and warning that the fuel and chemical costs could prove more than temporary. Governor Ueda separately hinted at a September move on September 2. Underneath the rhetoric: final Q2 GDP revised UP to +0.4% q/q from a 0.3% flash with annualised 1.4% against 1.1% expected, the Reuters Tankan at 21 from 18 against a 15 forecast, machine tool orders +64.7% y/y, average cash earnings +4.7% y/y - the fastest since 1997 - real wages positive for a seventh straight month, a current account swung to PLUS 2,989bn yen from MINUS 92.3bn, and retail sales +2.4% m/m. US Treasury Secretary Bessent has warned traders against betting against the yen and the Takaichi administration has acknowledged the need to limit excessive yen weakness; the yen also jumped to a one-month intraday high on September 3 as traders weighed intervention risk. The one caveat worth carrying is TE's July-meeting summary: the BoJ CUT its FY2026 inflation forecast to 2.5% from 2.8% on government energy relief, while raising FY2026 GDP to 0.6% and FY2027 inflation to 2.4% and growth to 0.8%. TE macro re-verified: CPI 1.9% with MoM 0.4%, jobless rate 2.4% from 2.5%, GDP 0.4% q/q and 0.7% y/y, business confidence 22 from 17, manufacturing PMI 54.9, services 52.5, consumer confidence 35.5. USD/JPY 153.716, +0.11% today but still -3.50% on the MONTH, the largest move of any major.

AUD.when: Sept 29, 04:30Z - market-implied near 54%, though TE's own consensus and forecast both sit at 4.35% for a hold
AUD.note: Cash rate re-verified on TE at 4.35%, the G10 high, held August 11. AUD HOLDS at +2, and today the reason for that score needs restating because the usual supporting argument just weakened. The commodity leg has turned: copper is 6.7356 USD per pound, DOWN 1.00% today with its monthly gain cut to +1.87% after this file quoted +2.90% on the week only yesterday. Silver fell 0.94% alongside it. The score is therefore held on the RATE DIFFERENTIAL and on domestic inflation persistence, not on commodities - that distinction matters for sizing and for how AUD crosses are expressed. What supports it: the G10-high 4.35% cash rate with September 29 near 54% market-implied; Melbourne Institute consumer inflation expectations UNCHANGED at 4.9% in September, elevated and sticky; trimmed mean stuck at 3.6%; and GDP annual growth at 2.1%, still above the RBA's estimated 2% speed limit. TE's summary of the August minutes remains the anchor - board members judged inflation TOO HIGH with excess demand persistent, staff projected target only by late 2027 with risks skewed upward, and the hike arguments were listed as Middle East conflict driving oil prices FIRST, then fuller cost pass-through, stronger AI and data-centre investment, resilient demand and weak productivity. Crude is +16.85% on the month with Brent above 102, so that first argument is stronger than when it was written even as copper fades. The underlying copper supply story is also intact - Codelco and Freeport double-digit declines, an ICSG-recorded 1.1% fall in global H1 output, a Congo export ban, weak Chilean and Peruvian supply - which is why XCU/USD keeps its LONG direction but loses conviction. Against all of it the domestic side stays genuinely soft and should keep being named: Westpac consumer confidence fell 5.2% to 84.4 and NAB business confidence slipped to MINUS 8 from MINUS 6. TE re-verified: headline CPI 3.5% from 3.8%, unemployment 4.5% from 4.4%, GDP 0.4% q/q from 0.3%, manufacturing PMI 52, services 53.2, balance of trade 1,923m from 2,341m. AUD/USD 0.72074, -0.14% today but +2.12% on the month, still the best major on the monthly horizon after the yen. AUD/NZD 1.2340.

NZD.when: Oct 28, 01:00Z is a pause on TE's own calendar; TE forecasts the next 25bp only on Dec 9, to 3.00%
NZD.note: OCR re-verified on TE at 2.75% after the September 2 hike from 2.50%. NZD HOLDS at MINUS 1 and today it is simply the worst major on the monthly horizon: NZD/USD is 0.58399, unchanged on the session and DOWN 0.65% on the month, the only major with a negative monthly return against the dollar. That confirms the withdrawal this file made yesterday of its claim that the kiwi's slide had stopped - that rebound was a one-session artefact and naming it as such was correct. The leg that justifies MINUS 1 has never depended on China. TE's own summary of the September 2 decision reads as a central bank explaining a hike in the past tense: removing stimulus gradually, annual inflation at 4.1% attributed LARGELY TO HIGHER FUEL PRICES FROM THE MIDDLE EAST CONFLICT, core inflation, wage growth and expectations all judged consistent with a return to the 1-3% band by mid-2027, and household spending weighed down by weak income growth, job insecurity and flat house prices. ANZ reads the statement as not pointing to an October increase, with the language around future decisions deliberately vague and highly conditional - which is why wholesale rates and the kiwi both FELL after a hike and AUD/NZD ran to its strongest since July on the decision itself. A central bank that raises to 2.75% and then declines to validate the next step does not get paid for its carry. TE carries October 28 unchanged with the next 25bp only on December 9. The domestic data is the worst in the G10 on second derivatives: TE re-verified unemployment 5.6% from 5.4%, the highest since Q3 2015; Q2 CPI 4.1% from 3.1%; GDP 0.8% q/q from 0.5% with annual growth 1.5%; consumer confidence 80.4 from 94.7, a collapse; manufacturing PMI 54.3 from 60.1; business confidence 53.7 from 56.1; balance of trade -1,949m from -237m; retail sales -0.5% m/m. It stays at MINUS 1 rather than MINUS 2 only because a majority of MPC members still see upside inflation risks and TE forecasts a December hike.

CAD.when: Oct 28 with the MPR - held for a seventh straight meeting on Sept 2, and August's job loss keeps the next move out
CAD.note: Policy rate re-verified on TE at 2.25%, held September 2. CAD HOLDS at +1, and the uncomfortable observation from yesterday not only stands but got worse. Brent is 102.167 and WTI 97.269, +1.27% today and +16.85% on the month - the strongest terms-of-trade impulse of the entire cycle - and USD/CAD is 1.38134, UP another 0.06% and weaker than yesterday's 1.38060. The oil-CAD beta is broken and this file will keep describing the position that way rather than repeating an oil thesis the currency refuses to pay. What the market is actually trading is the labour leg: August employment fell 41,700 against a +15,000 consensus after +75,100, full-time down 36,000, and average hourly wages decelerated to 2.0% y/y from 2.8% in July and 3.3% in June. A 2.0% wage run-rate is not consistent with the inflation persistence the September 2 statement worries about, which is what keeps the next move past October 28. The growth data is genuinely strong and TE re-verified it: current account PLUS C$8,800m from MINUS 8,300m, business confidence 64.3 from 55.1, Q2 GDP 0.8% q/q from 0.1% with annual growth 1.1% from 0.1% and an annualised 3.3% from 0.3%. TE's summary of the September statement notes a broad Q2 recovery with resilience to the war, stronger UPSIDE inflation risks from both the continuation of the war and the reintroduction of aggressive US tariffs, underlying inflation still holding at target despite the energy shock, and an uncertain outlook preventing any clear policy signal this year. TE also re-verified CPI 3.0% with MoM 0.5%, unemployment 6.4%, manufacturing PMI 53, consumer confidence 48.2, retail sales -0.8% m/m, balance of trade 770m from 4,200m. The C$27.6bn of counter-tariffs across roughly 700 US product lines are in force. Keep every CAD expression low-conviction until the currency starts trading its own terms of trade again.

CHF.when: Sept 24, 07:30Z - TE carries a 0% consensus and a 0% forecast; nothing this week changes the base case
CHF.note: Policy rate re-verified on TE at 0.00%, held March 19 and again June 18. CHF HOLDS at +1, and the franc has now failed its haven test for a SECOND consecutive session. USD/CHF is 0.81110, up 0.12% today, leaving the franc flat on the month at -0.03% - through an overnight period that included the largest escalation of the war so far, a US tanker-for-tanker policy sinking five Iranian vessels, Iranian strikes on 10 ships and on the Al-Azraq base in Jordan, and an IAEA referral to the UN Security Council. Two days ago this file argued the franc was gaining a second bid as the cleanest European hedge against the gas shock. That argument is not visible in the price and is now retired rather than merely held loosely: from here the franc is expressed on DATA AND DIFFERENTIALS ONLY, never as a haven. The data remains outstanding and TE re-verified it: August CPI 0.8% y/y with MoM +0.4%, the fastest since August 2024; Q2 GDP +1.5% q/q with ANNUAL growth 2.3% from 0.4%, the strongest since Q3 2021; unemployment 3.0%; manufacturing PMI 57.1 from 53.2, a large jump; business confidence 107 from 104; current account CHF 15,544m from 2,994m; balance of trade 8,141m from 3,834m; retail sales +0.1% m/m. On data alone this is a +2. What caps it is explicit and TE-verified: the SNB forecasts annual average inflation of just 0.6% for 2026 and 2027 and 0.7% for 2028 with growth of 1% in 2026 and 1.5% in 2027, said in June that medium-term inflation pressures remain LARGELY UNCHANGED despite energy-driven price increases, highlighted Middle East tensions as potentially strengthening the franc, and signalled a GREATER READINESS TO INTERVENE in foreign exchange markets. With the war escalating and the franc still not bid, that intervention language is very likely to be repeated on September 24 and there is nothing forcing the SNB to move. Keep every CHF cross at MEDIUM or below and do not buy a hawkish SNB.

strength.drivers: TE's calendar carries consensus 1% but its OWN forecast at 1.25% for the September 18 BoJ; board member Masu said the Bank expects to CONTINUE raising rates and that further hikes avoid being forced into rapid tightening later, after Ueda hinted at a September move on September 2; final Q2 GDP revised up to +0.4% q/q with annualised 1.4% against 1.1% expected, Reuters Tankan 21 from 18 against a 15 forecast, machine tool orders +64.7% y/y, average cash earnings +4.7% y/y - the fastest since 1997 - real wages positive for a seventh month, current account PLUS 2,989bn yen; policy rate 1.00%, CPI 1.9%, jobless rate 2.4% from 2.5%; USD/JPY 153.716, -3.50% on the month, the largest move of any major.
strength.forward: 🦅 Tightening, and on a day when gold, silver, copper and the franc all failed their respective tests the yen is again the only currency actually paying. Masu's framing is what matters more than the headline: hawkish on direction, deliberate on pace - the gradual-but-continuous path that appreciates the yen without inviting MoF pushback. He named Iran-driven fuel and chemical costs, distribution and food costs, yen pass-through and AI demand as persistent pressures, and warned the fuel component may be more than temporary. With September 18 largely spoken for and TE forecasting the hike outright, the yen gets paid on GUIDANCE and on the roughly 75bp of cumulative tightening swaps carry through April 2027. Bessent's warning against betting against the currency and the Takaichi administration's stated intent to limit excessive weakness sit underneath it, and the yen touched a one-month intraday high on September 3 on intervention risk alone. Invalidated by a hike-and-explicit-pause, or by MoF discomfort at the PACE after a 3.50% monthly move.

strength.tag: Held on rates, NOT on copper
strength.drivers: Cash rate 4.35%, the G10 high, with September 29 near 54% market-implied; Melbourne Institute consumer inflation expectations UNCHANGED at 4.9% in September; trimmed mean stuck at 3.6% with headline CPI 3.5% from 3.8%; GDP 0.4% q/q from 0.3% and 2.1% y/y, above the RBA's estimated 2% speed limit; unemployment 4.5% from 4.4% - against a commodity leg that TURNED today, with copper 6.7356 and DOWN 1.00%, its monthly gain cut to +1.87% from the +2.90% weekly figure quoted yesterday, and silver -0.94%; AUD/USD 0.72074, -0.14% today but +2.12% on the month.
strength.forward: 🦅 Tightening bias, but the basis of the score has narrowed and that should be stated plainly rather than glossed. Until today AUD rested on two legs - the G10-high policy rate and the commodity complex. The commodity leg has weakened: copper fell 1.00% and halved its monthly gain in a single session, silver fell with it, and the reason is the same US real-rate repricing that took gold below 4,400. The rate leg is untouched and is doing all the work: inflation expectations at 4.9% are exactly the persistence the August minutes flagged when they judged inflation TOO HIGH with excess demand and staff seeing target only by late 2027, and those minutes list Middle East oil FIRST among hike arguments - with crude +16.85% on the month, that argument is stronger than when written. The underlying copper SUPPLY story also still holds: Codelco and Freeport double-digit declines, an ICSG-recorded 1.1% fall in H1 output, a Congo export ban. Invalidated by a second consecutive soft copper session combined with another weak domestic print - Westpac consumer confidence at 84.4 after a 5.2% fall and NAB business confidence at MINUS 8 remain the honest counterweight - which would take this to +1.

strength.tag: Decision day, projections are the event
strength.drivers: ECB decides TODAY at 12:15Z with the deposit facility going 2.25% to 2.50% at 99% priced and TE consensus and forecast at 2.65% on the refi; TE states interest-rate futures price a THIRD hike by December, with previews near 40-50%; flash HICP 3.3%, the highest since September 2023, with ENERGY inflation 14.3% from 10.3% and core 2.4%; Q2 GDP +0.6% q/q and 1.2% y/y; unemployment 6.4%; manufacturing PMI 52.7 from 51.9, services 51.6, composite 52; wage growth 3.4% from 3.1% - against EU gas at 80.30 euros per MWh, +36.58% on the month, German gas +4.42% in a single session to 80.40, and German storage at 53%; EUR/USD 1.16318.
strength.forward: ⚖️ Balanced with a HAWKISH tilt into the 12:15Z decision, and the asymmetry is worth naming precisely. The 25bp is 99% priced so it carries no information; the new STAFF PROJECTIONS do. August energy inflation at 14.3% was collected BEFORE the latest gas leg, and TTF has risen further since - so the staff inflation path can be revised UP into a market that had decided the cycle was finished, and TE says futures already price a third hike by December at roughly 40-50%. This file called the path CLOSED two days ago on the September 3 Reuters poll and was wrong; rate-market pricing outranks an economist poll and the correction stands. Against the hawkish case: TE notes the ECB is expected to signal caution about increases that could weigh on activity, that there are still few signs of the second-round effects policymakers fear, and that economists warn further tightening risks recession - plus the gas shock is a terms-of-trade TAX no hike offsets, with Morgan Stanley now seeing ~85 euro TTF this winter and no Qatari return. Invalidated upward by higher staff projections plus December kept explicitly live; downward by Lagarde naming 2.50% as terminal while gas compounds.

strength.drivers: CME FedWatch drifted to 58% from 56% for a 25bp move to 4.00% on September 16, which is also TE's own forecast, having been 58.7% on September 7 and 66% on August 31 after Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks; August payrolls +162,000 against +53,000 expected with the prior two months revised up by a combined 55,000; unemployment 4.1%, CPI 3.4% with MoM 0.1%, GDP 2.1% annual, non-manufacturing PMI 55.4 and services 56.5 - against consumer confidence 51.7 and retail sales -0.6% m/m; policy rate 3.75% upper bound; DXY 98.830, +0.01% today and -1.03% on the month.
strength.forward: ⚖️ Balanced and dormant in FX - but the hawkish repricing is expressing itself somewhere, and that is the useful observation today. A 56% to 58% drift is inside a range this file has already traded and CoinDesk argued explicitly on September 7 that the payrolls beat did NOT materially move Fed pricing, so the USD score does not flip on it and DXY is still -1.03% on the month. Yet gold broke below 4,400 and silver fell 0.94% on the same repricing: rising US real rates are beating the war bid on every asset that pays no coupon. So the tradeable expression of a hawkish Fed right now is SHORT METALS, not long dollars. TE's summary of the July minutes supports the direction - officials concerned about persistent inflation, several judging financial conditions possibly not restrictive enough, a small group wanting an immediate hike, inflation risks tilted to the UPSIDE - though the meeting predated the cooler employment and inflation data. Prediction markets stay lower at 48-49% and are not rate-market pricing. Hold USD/JPY as a JAPAN trade with a neutral dollar leg. Invalidated in either direction by PPI today at 12:30Z and August CPI tomorrow at 12:30Z, consensus 3.4%.

strength.drivers: Brent 102.167 and WTI 97.269, +1.27% today and +16.85% on the month, the strongest terms-of-trade impulse of the cycle - and USD/CAD is 1.38134, UP 0.06% today and weaker than yesterday's 1.38060; current account PLUS C$8,800m from MINUS 8,300m; business confidence 64.3 from 55.1; Q2 GDP 0.8% q/q, 1.1% y/y and 3.3% annualised from 0.3% - against August employment MINUS 41,700 with average hourly wages decelerating to 2.0% y/y from 2.8% in July and 3.3% in June, CPI 3.0%, unemployment 6.4%, and the policy rate held at 2.25% for a seventh meeting.
strength.forward: ⚖️ Balanced, and the broken transmission observed yesterday not only persists but extended - crude rose again and the loonie weakened again. Repeating an oil thesis the currency refuses to pay would be exactly the stale-call problem this file exists to avoid, so the honest position is that the crude view belongs in USOIL directly, not in CAD. What the market is actually trading is the labour leg: a 2.0% wage run-rate is not consistent with the inflation persistence the September 2 statement worries about, which is what pushes the next move past October 28. The growth data is genuinely the best in months and the BoC does flag stronger upside inflation risks from both the continuing war and renewed US tariffs, while noting underlying inflation has held at target despite the energy shock - that is what keeps the score positive rather than neutral. Invalidated upward by the oil beta re-engaging plus any labour stabilisation; downward by damage from the C$27.6bn of counter-tariffs now in force across roughly 700 US product lines.

strength.drivers: A SECOND consecutive session with no haven bid - USD/CHF 0.81110, +0.12% today, leaving the franc at -0.03% on the month through a US tanker-for-tanker escalation, Iranian strikes on 10 ships and the Al-Azraq base in Jordan, and an IAEA referral to the Security Council; against outstanding data: manufacturing PMI 57.1 from 53.2, current account CHF 15,544m from 2,994m, business confidence 107 from 104, balance of trade 8,141m from 3,834m; August CPI 0.8% y/y with MoM +0.4%, the fastest since August 2024; Q2 GDP +1.5% q/q with annual growth 2.3% from 0.4%, the strongest since Q3 2021; unemployment 3.0%; policy rate 0.00%.
strength.forward: ⚖️ Balanced and capped - on the data alone this would be a +2. The change today is a retirement rather than a re-score: two days ago this file argued the franc was gaining a second bid as the cleanest European hedge against the gas shock, yesterday it held that loosely, and after a second session in which the largest escalation of the war produced no franc strength at all, the haven argument is dropped outright. From here CHF is expressed on data and differentials only. The ceiling is explicit and TE-verified: the SNB forecasts annual average inflation of just 0.6% for 2026 and 2027 and 0.7% for 2028, said in June that medium-term pressures remain largely unchanged despite energy-driven increases, named Middle East tensions as a franc-strengthening risk, and signalled a GREATER READINESS TO INTERVENE. With the franc still not bid through an escalating war, that intervention language is very likely repeated on September 24. Invalidated upward only if the SNB drops the intervention language; downward by a reversion in the October 1 CPI.

strength.drivers: UK gas 200.38 pence per therm, +1.37% today and +38.71% on the MONTH - up from +36.33% yesterday and +29.82% the day before, the worst gas exposure in G10 - into a confirmed October Ofgem cap rise; Bank Rate 3.75% with September 17 about 90% priced for no change and a 0/9 TE vote-cut consensus; July government borrowing 69% above the prior year; CPI 2.9% with core 2.6%; GDP 0.4% q/q from 0.6% with annual growth 1.2%; wage growth 4.1% from 4.4%; employment change +83k from +147k; retail sales +1.6% y/y from 3.8%; cable 1.35421, -0.04% today but +0.32% on the month.
strength.forward: 🔻 Easing-relative, held on structure and now on a third consecutive session of energy deterioration. A 38.71% monthly gas move into an October cap rise is STAGFLATIONARY for a Bank already frozen: it lifts the CPI path while cutting real household income, and TE's own read of the July decision is a Bank that expects inflation to RISE later this year on energy while labour conditions weaken, sees little second-round evidence, and stands ready to tighten but will not. The structural leg is unchanged - the highest borrowing costs of any G10 developed nation, borrowing 69% above prior year, and a yield advantage that fails to attract capital because it is risk premium rather than carry. The momentum caveat also stands and keeps this honest: cable is +0.32% on the MONTH, so the short is not paying against the dollar and GBP/USD stays LOW-MED. Express sterling against the YEN and the EURO, where the differential story is unambiguous. Invalidated by a hard upside surprise in tomorrow's monthly GDP at 06:00Z, or by a credible fiscal statement.

strength.tag: Only major negative on the month
strength.drivers: NZD/USD 0.58399, flat on the session and DOWN 0.65% on the MONTH - the only major with a negative monthly return against the dollar; OCR 2.75% after the September 2 hike, with TE carrying October 28 unchanged and the next 25bp only on December 9; unemployment 5.6% from 5.4%, the highest since Q3 2015; Q2 CPI 4.1% from 3.1%, which the RBNZ attributes largely to Middle East fuel prices; consumer confidence 80.4 from 94.7, a collapse; manufacturing PMI 54.3 from 60.1; business confidence 53.7 from 56.1; balance of trade -1,949m from -237m.
strength.forward: 🔻 Easing-relative, and the monthly numbers now settle the argument this file had with itself over the last two sessions. It reported a rebound on Monday, withdrew that yesterday as a one-day artefact, and today the kiwi is the ONLY major down against the dollar on the month. The leg that justified MINUS 1 never depended on China: it is a central bank that raised to 2.75% and then declined to validate the next step. ANZ reads the September 2 statement as not pointing to an October increase, with the language around future decisions deliberately vague and highly conditional, which is why wholesale rates and the kiwi both FELL after a hike and AUD/NZD ran to its strongest since July on the decision itself. A central bank that hikes and then refuses to guide does not get paid for its carry. The second-derivative data is the worst in G10 - consumer confidence down 14 points, manufacturing PMI down almost 6 - and TE carries no move until December 9. It stays at MINUS 1 rather than MINUS 2 only because a majority of MPC members still see upside inflation risks and TE does forecast that December hike. Invalidated if October 28 pulls the December move forward, or if the RBNZ hardens on the 4.1% headline it currently blames on Middle East fuel.

symbols.why: The widest differential on the board: a BoJ that TE forecasts at 1.25% on September 18 against an RBNZ that hiked to 2.75% and then refused to validate the next step, with TE carrying no move until December 9. NZD is the only major negative on the month at -0.65% while JPY is -3.50% against USD.
symbols.risk: A hawkish RBNZ surprise on October 28 pulling the December hike forward, or a BoJ hike-and-explicit-pause on September 18.

symbols.why: Sterling carries the worst energy exposure in G10 with UK gas now +38.71% on the month into an October Ofgem cap rise, against a Bank frozen at 3.75% with a 0/9 vote-cut consensus - versus the only central bank whose next hike is already in TE's own forecast.
symbols.risk: A hard upside surprise in UK monthly GDP tomorrow at 06:00Z, or MoF discomfort at the pace of yen appreciation.

symbols.why: The basket rises as JPY strengthens and JPY is the only uncompromised +3 on the board: TE forecasts 1.25% on September 18, Masu says the Bank expects to keep raising to avoid forced rapid tightening later, and cash earnings are +4.7% y/y, the fastest since 1997.
symbols.risk: A hike-and-pause on September 18, or intervention-style jawboning inverted to the strong side if the pace alarms the MoF.

symbols.risk: A hot August CPI tomorrow at 12:30Z that converts the 58% into a near-certainty and lifts the dollar leg materially.

symbols.why: The cleanest antipodean spread and the trade least affected by today's commodity turn: RBA at a G10-high 4.35% with inflation expectations stuck at 4.9% and September 29 near 54%, against an RBNZ on hold until December. Spot 1.2340, strongest since July.
symbols.risk: A dovish RBA turn on September 29, or an RBNZ that hardens its October 28 language on the 4.1% headline.

symbols.why: An ECB hiking today with futures pricing a third move by December at 40-50%, against a Bank of England that TE shows holding on September 17 with a 0/9 vote-cut consensus - and sterling carries the worse gas exposure of the two at +38.71% versus +36.58% monthly.
symbols.risk: Lagarde naming 2.50% as terminal at 12:45Z, which would close the December path and unwind the spread.

symbols.why: The only asset still carrying the war premium and it keeps extending: WTI 97.269, +1.27% today and +16.85% on the month, with a US tanker-for-tanker policy live after Washington sank five Iranian tankers and Iran struck 10 ships plus the Al-Azraq base in Jordan. Take the crude view here, not through CAD.
symbols.risk: A credible de-escalation or ceasefire signal, or an OPEC+ supply response large enough to offset the Hormuz risk premium.

symbols.why: German gas jumped 4.42% in a single session to 80.40 euros per MWh and is +29.43% on the month with storage only 53% full, into an ECB tightening at 12:15Z and a war escalating - three simultaneous headwinds for an energy-intensive index.
symbols.risk: Falling Brent, or a dovish Lagarde naming 2.50% as terminal, which would relieve both the energy and the policy legs at once.

symbols.why: Pairs the strongest forward tilt in Europe - an ECB hiking today with December alive at 40-50% - against the weakest in the G10, an RBNZ with nothing until December 9 and the only major negative monthly return against the dollar.
symbols.risk: A dovish ECB press conference at 12:45Z, or an RBNZ that surprises hawkish on October 28.

symbols.why: Both central banks are tightening, so this is a relative-pace trade and the yen wins it: TE forecasts the BoJ hike outright on September 18 while the euro leg carries a gas TAX at +36.58% monthly that no ECB hike offsets.
symbols.risk: Materially higher ECB staff projections today plus December kept explicitly live, which would close the pace gap.

symbols.why: A franc that has now failed its haven test for a second straight session at a 0.00% policy rate, against a yen whose next hike is in TE's own forecast. Two would-be havens, only one with a central bank behind it.
symbols.risk: SNB dropping its intervention language on September 24, or a BoJ pause that removes the yen's rate leg.

symbols.why: The broken oil beta makes this cleaner than it looks: Brent above 102 and the loonie still weakened, so CAD is not being paid for the terms-of-trade impulse, while August wages at 2.0% y/y keep the BoC out past October 28 against a BoJ hiking.
symbols.risk: The oil-CAD beta re-engaging sharply, which would give the CAD leg a delayed catch-up bid.

symbols.why: The kiwi is the only major with a negative monthly return against the dollar at -0.65%, on an RBNZ that hiked and then refused to guide, unemployment at 5.6% and consumer confidence collapsing from 94.7 to 80.4.
symbols.risk: A soft August US CPI tomorrow that knocks the 58% Fed pricing down and lifts every dollar-denominated major.

symbols.why: Sells the weakest currency on the board against one with strong growth data, a current account swung to +C$8,800m and business confidence at 64.3 from 55.1 - even with the oil leg discounted to zero.
symbols.risk: Renewed US tariff damage to Canada under the C$27.6bn counter-tariff regime, or a hawkish RBNZ shift.

symbols.why: Expresses the kiwi weakness against the franc on Swiss DATA rather than on any haven claim - manufacturing PMI 57.1 from 53.2, annual GDP 2.3% and a current account of CHF 15,544m - which is the only CHF argument this file still holds.
symbols.risk: SNB intervention rhetoric on September 24 capping the franc, keeping this range-bound rather than trending.

symbols.why: Sterling's +38.71% monthly gas shock and frozen Bank against Canada's best growth data in months; even with the loonie not paying its oil beta, the relative energy exposure runs clearly the other way - Canada is a net exporter of the shock.
symbols.risk: Weak UK GDP being already priced, or further tariff damage weighing on CAD independently.

symbols.why: The G10 worst gas exposure and highest borrowing costs against Swiss data that would justify a +2 in isolation: CPI 0.8%, annual GDP 2.3%, unemployment 3.0% and a manufacturing PMI at 57.1.
symbols.risk: SNB intervention readiness capping the franc leg, plus sterling short covering after tomorrow's GDP.

symbols.why: A frozen Bank of England against the G10-high 4.35% cash rate with September 29 near 54% - and this expression is insulated from today's copper turn because the Australian score now rests on the rate leg, not commodities.
symbols.risk: A further slide in copper combined with soft Australian employment, which would take AUD to +1 and flatten the spread.

symbols.why: Direction held on a genuine physical shortage - Codelco and Freeport double-digit declines, an ICSG-recorded 1.1% fall in global H1 output, a Congo export ban, weak Chilean and Peruvian supply - but conviction CUT from MEDIUM after a 1.00% fall to 6.7356 halved the monthly gain to +1.87%.
symbols.risk: The US real-rate repricing that took gold below 4,400 spreading further into industrial metals; a second soft session would argue for RANGE.

symbols.risk: The clear stretch trade on this board: an RBA that turns explicitly hawkish on September 29 would make this the wrong side.

symbols.why: The structural sterling case is intact - worst G10 gas exposure, highest borrowing costs, borrowing 69% above prior year - but the pair keeps refusing to pay, so conviction stays capped.
symbols.risk: Cable is still +0.32% on the MONTH at 1.35421; the short has not worked against the dollar and a soft US CPI tomorrow would hurt it further.

symbols.why: Two hawkish central banks with Australia holding the rate advantage at 4.35% versus a 2.50% deposit facility after today, but the euro leg is live at 12:15Z and the Australian commodity leg just turned, so both sides are unsettled.
symbols.risk: Materially higher ECB staff projections keeping December live, into further copper weakness on the AUD side.

symbols.why: Still +2.12% on the month and the best major after the yen, on the G10-high cash rate and inflation expectations stuck at 4.9% - but it fell 0.14% today as copper turned, and the commodity leg is no longer supporting it.
symbols.risk: A hot US CPI tomorrow converting 58% Fed pricing into near-certainty, compounding the commodity fade.

symbols.why: The rate differential is stark at 4.35% against 2.25% with the BoC out past October 28 on 2.0% wage growth - but both currencies are commodity-linked and both commodity legs are behaving oddly right now.
symbols.risk: The oil-CAD beta re-engaging with Brent above 102 would flip this quickly given the size of the terms-of-trade impulse.

symbols.why: The widest policy gap available at 4.35% against 0.00%, with the franc now demonstrably not bid as a haven through two sessions of war escalation.
symbols.risk: Australian commodity weakness extending while Swiss data stays outstanding, or SNB rhetoric that is read hawkishly on September 24.

symbols.why: DOWNGRADED from LONG today. Silver was held as gold with an extra industrial leg; today it fell 0.94% to 66.634 while copper fell 1.00%, so the industrial leg is precisely what broke and the reason to prefer silver over gold has gone. It joins gold at RANGE.
symbols.risk: The +3.03% monthly gain is still the best in the metals complex, so a dovish US CPI tomorrow could restore both the haven and the industrial legs at once.

symbols.risk: A resolution in either direction - the oil beta re-engaging, or a hot US CPI that finally gives the dollar leg a trend.

symbols.why: A franc that will not bid as a haven against a dollar that is dormant in FX despite 58% hike pricing. Spot 0.81110 with the franc flat on the month at -0.03%; nothing is trending here.
symbols.risk: August US CPI tomorrow at 12:30Z is the only near-term catalyst capable of giving either leg direction.

symbols.why: A hiking ECB against strong Canadian growth data, with the euro carrying a gas tax and the loonie refusing to trade its own terms of trade. Both legs are compromised in opposite ways.
symbols.risk: A decisive ECB press conference at 12:45Z, or the oil-CAD beta re-engaging, would break the range.

symbols.why: 98.830, +0.01% today and -1.03% on the month. The 58% Fed pricing is expressing itself in gold and silver rather than in the dollar index, and the EUR weight of 57.6% is frozen until 12:15Z.

geopolitics: The war escalated again overnight and the FX market again declined to price it, which is now the single most reliable feature of this regime. The United States is operating an explicit tanker-for-tanker policy approved by President Trump: Washington sank five Iranian oil tankers in the Gulf of Oman and near Kharg Island after accusing Tehran of firing ballistic missiles at a US warship, and Iran retaliated by attacking 10 ships near the Strait of Hormuz and firing missiles at US forces at the Al-Azraq base in Jordan. That follows the extension of Iran's prohibited zone beyond the Strait into the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea, and an IAEA referral of Iran to the UN Security Council. TradingEconomics now describes the Strait as closed by the war in its own ECB commentary, which is the framing the ECB will be working from at 12:15Z. The transmission is entirely through energy and it is intensifying rather than fading: WTI is 97.269 and +1.27% today for +16.85% on the month, Brent is 102.167 and +14.82% monthly having broken 100 dollars on Wednesday, Urals is 95.74 and +16.94%, heating oil is +11.70%, coal +14.22%, LNG JKM +16.11%, and the European gas complex is the worst affected with EU gas at 80.30 euros per MWh and +36.58% monthly, German gas jumping 4.42% in a single session to 80.40 and +29.43% monthly, and UK gas at 200.38 pence per therm and +38.71% monthly. What is genuinely new today is that the FX and metals havens are not merely flat but actively falling. Gold has broken below 4,400 to 4,392.69 with only +0.54% left on the month, silver fell 0.94%, copper fell 1.00%, and the Swiss franc weakened for a second straight session with USD/CHF at 0.81110. The explanation is US real rates: CME FedWatch pricing for a September 16 Fed hike has drifted to 58% with TradingEconomics forecasting 4.00% outright, and a rising discount rate beats a geopolitical bid on every asset that pays no coupon. The FX read follows directly. Own the war through USOIL, where the premium actually accrues, and short GER40, where the energy tax lands on an index that cannot pass it through. Do NOT own the war through CAD - Brent above 102 has produced a weaker loonie two sessions running - and do NOT own it through gold, silver or the franc, all three of which have now failed the same test. The one currency that keeps paying is the yen, and it is paying for a reason unrelated to the war: the Bank of Japan is the only central bank on this board whose next hike sits in TradingEconomics own forecast. De-escalation is the main risk to USOIL, to GER40 short, and to the euro-area energy tax; it would do comparatively little to the yen trade, which is why the yen remains the cleanest expression on the board.
